moment.text: When the children of Israel saw it, they said to one another, “What is it?” For they didn’t know what it was. Moses said to them, “It is the bread which Yahweh has given you to eat.

previous.text: When the dew that lay had gone, behold, on the surface of the wilderness was a small round thing, small as the frost on the ground.

next.text: This is the thing which Yahweh has commanded: ‘Gather of it everyone according to his eating; an omer a head, according to the number of your persons, you shall take it, every man for those who are in his tent.’”

payload.title: Quail and manna appear; rules for gathering

payload.name: Moses
payload.note: Israel's lawgiver and leader who led the people out of Egypt, received the law at Sinai and is named across the Old and New Testament divisions as the same individual, distinguished only by the sections in which he appears or is mentioned.

stages.label: Moses, elder

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

stages.text: Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.

stages.label: Moses, infant

quotes.quote: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

stages.text: Moses: a newborn infant; soft smooth skin; a small round face; a little dark hair; wrapped in plain linen cloth and laid in a woven reed basket sealed with bitumen and pitch; no beard, no staff, no adult clothing.

stages.label: Moses, adult

quotes.quote: But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

stages.text: Moses: a man of about forty; lean, strong, well-proportioned build; brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard; alert, sober face; a knee-length undyed linen tunic with a dark woven wool cloak of brown and grey pinned at the shoulder; he carries a plain wooden shepherd's staff.

payload.name: Aaron, brother of Moses
payload.note: Moses' older brother and first high priest, in Exodus and in Numbers (census, offerings, death on Mount Hor); the same man across both divisions.

stages.label: Aaron, the first high priest

quotes.quote: Amram took Jochebed his father’s sister to himself as wife; and she bore him Aaron and Moses.
Of the blue, purple, and scarlet, they made finely worked garments for ministering in the holy place, and made the holy garments for Aaron
Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.

stages.text: Aaron: man in his eighties, older brother of Moses; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and close-cropped hair; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a blue robe, a woven ephod of blue, purple and scarlet, a breastplate, and a linen headband. Props: none carried alone; the rod of the Exodus is sometimes held.

aliases: those who came out of Egypt
payload.name: The Israelite people (the children of Israel)
payload.note: The collective Israelite nation across Exodus through Malachi and Hebrews, one body whose different portrayals (marching nation, assembly, covenant people, judged northern kingdom, returned community, wilderness generation) are all the same people; distinguish only from the returned community of Nehemiah in the note by the Judah/Jerusalem setting, but these are the same people.

stages.label: The Israelite people

quotes.quote: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt
You shall tell the children of Israel this
So they shall put my name on the children of Israel; and I will bless them.

stages.text: The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.

aliases: the God of our Lord Jesus Christ
him who sits on the throne
payload.name: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel
payload.note: The one God, creator and speaker of the Old Testament and the Father of Jesus Christ in the New Testament; distinct from Jesus in every entry.

stages.label: God the Father (radiance and cloud)

quotes.quote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.

stages.text: God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

payload.name: The wilderness (Exodus route)
payload.note: The desert stretches Israel travels from Egypt through Shur, Sin and Marah, with manna, quail and water miracles; the same wilderness as the Psalms and Amos references.

stages.label: The wilderness (Exodus route)

quotes.quote: they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water.
on the surface of the wilderness was a small round thing, small as the frost on the ground.
in a dry and weary land, where there is no water.

stages.text: The wilderness: a vast arid tableland of pale sand, gravel plains and dark rock outcrops rising to bare mountains, scattered with thorn scrub and sparse grasses in the wadis. Tents and camp-circles mark the encampments; a distant mountain, Sinai, rises above the plain. Dry riverbeds, stone wells and rock fissures suggest hidden water.

aliases: the tent of meeting outside the camp
payload.name: the camp of Israel
payload.note: The Israelite encampment in the wilderness, with the tent of meeting set outside it in Exodus 33; the same encampment that Leviticus calls the camp.

stages.label: the camp of Israel

quotes.quote: the pillar of cloud moved from before them, and stood behind them.
quail came up and covered the camp; and in the morning the dew lay around the camp.
Moses used to take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, far away from the camp
outside of the camp to a clean place where the ashes are poured out

stages.text: the camp of Israel: a wide wilderness encampment of dun-coloured tents of woven goat-hair cloth in ordered rows, with a central sanctuary tent and a gate; bare stony desert plain, scattered acacia and tamarisk, distant dark mountain slopes; a pillar of cloud above the camp by day and fire by night; ash-pits and a clean place beyond its edges.

moment.text: The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening; and he drank from the brook.

previous.text: So he went and did according to Yahweh’s word, for he went and lived by the brook Cherith that is before the Jordan.

next.text: After a while, the brook dried up, because there was no rain in the land.

aliases: the man of God on the hill
payload.name: Elijah
payload.note: Tishbite prophet of Gilead who confronts Ahab, calls fire on Carmel and is taken up by a whirlwind; the same prophet in 1 Kings and 2 Kings, rebuking Ahaziah and parting the Jordan.

stages.label: Elijah

quotes.quote: He was a hairy man, and wearing a leather belt around his waist.
Elijah the Tishbite, who was one of the settlers of Gilead
Elijah took his mantle, and rolled it up, and struck the waters

stages.text: Elijah: a lean, weathered man of middle years; sinewy build, tall and spare; sun-darkened skin; long, unkempt hair and a full wild beard; deep-set, unflinching eyes. Signature outfit in dark brown sheepskin mantle over a rough undertunic, girded with a plain leather belt; colours of earth, umber and ash. Carries only his mantle, which he rolls and strikes with.

payload.name: Cherith
payload.note: Brook east of the Jordan where ravens feed Elijah.

stages.label: Cherith

quotes.quote: hide yourself by the brook Cherith, that is before the Jordan
lived by the brook Cherith that is before the Jordan

stages.text: Cherith: a narrow wadi brook running east of the Jordan through a dry, rocky ravine. Steep limestone banks rise on both sides, cut by ledges and caves. Thin oleanders, tamarisk and scrub grow along the water's edge, with oleander and reeds in the damp channel. Sparse dry grass and scattered boulders cover the slopes.

payload.name: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord
payload.note: The one Jesus: the teacher from Nazareth of the Gospels and Acts, and the risen, exalted Christ and Lord of the epistles and Revelation; the same individual across all divisions, with death, resurrection and changed portrayal not creating new individuals.

stages.label: Adult Jesus

quotes.quote: Jesus himself, when he began to teach, was about thirty years old, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli,

stages.text: Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.

stages.label: Infant Jesus

quotes.quote: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.

stages.text: Jesus: newborn to about two years old; olive-brown skin, a little dark hair and dark eyes; a small infant or toddler's build, no beard. Plain undyed swaddling linen for the newborn; a small plain linen tunic as a toddler. No adult clothing or props.

stages.label: Boy Jesus

quotes.quote: When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast;

stages.text: Jesus: boy of about twelve, slim and sturdy; olive-brown skin; dark brown hair cut short at the neck; dark eyes; no beard; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak; no props.

payload.name: The Twelve Disciples (collective)
payload.note: The twelve apostles/disciples as one collective body acting together across the Gospels and Acts; distinct from the individual disciples named within them.

stages.label: The Twelve Disciples (collective)

quotes.quote: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these. The first, Simon, who is called Peter; Andrew, his brother; James the son of Zebedee
One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to him,

stages.text: The Twelve Disciples: men of about twenty to forty years; sun-browned, lean and sturdy from fishing and walking; olive to weathered brown skin; short or shoulder-length dark hair and close-trimmed beards; plain, earnest faces. Signature outfit: a undyed linen tunic and a rough brown wool cloak with fringed hem. Signature props: a fishing net coiled over one shoulder for Peter and Andrew; a walking staff for travelers.

payload.name: Judea (Gospel region around Jerusalem)
payload.note: The southern Jewish region around Jerusalem named in Mark and Luke, where Herod reigns and crowds come to John and Jesus; the Luke entry includes the hill country of Judea and the Roman province.

stages.label: Judea, the hill country around Jerusalem

quotes.quote: All the country of Judea and all those of Jerusalem went out to him.
Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.
all these sayings were talked about throughout all the hill country of Judea.

stages.text: Judea: rolling limestone hill country of terraced slopes, dry scrub and olive groves, stone-walled fields and winding dirt roads. Villages of pale cut-stone houses with flat roofs, a few synagogues of dressed stone, and Jerusalem's walls and temple mount rising on the skyline. Stony wilderness and mountains lie east toward the Jordan valley. Olive, fig and terebinth trees, sparse grass.

payload.name: The Samaritan woman at the well
payload.note: Unnamed woman of Sychar who meets Jesus at Jacob's well and believes in John.

stages.label: The Samaritan woman at the well

quotes.quote: How is it that you, being a Jew, ask for a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?

stages.text: The Samaritan woman at the well: a woman of about thirty, of slender, steady build, with warm olive-brown skin weathered by sun and daily labour. Her dark hair is pulled back under a plain linen head covering in faded ochre. Her face is calm and perceptive, with dark eyes and a firm, serious mouth. Her signature outfit is a long undyed linen tunic in earth brown under a dusty blue-grey wool cloak. She carries a clay water jar on her shoulder.

payload.name: Sychar
payload.note: The Samaritan town by Jacob's well where Jesus speaks with the woman in John; a town, not the capital city or the wider region of Samaria.

stages.label: Sychar

quotes.quote: a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph
A woman of Samaria came to draw water.

stages.text: Sychar: a small hill town of Samaria on rising ground, its pale limestone houses flat-roofed and clustered close, with narrow lanes and a stone wall at the edge. Olive trees, fig and terebinth grow on the terraced slopes below. Nearby lies the fertile field given by Jacob to Joseph, with an old stone-lined well of Jacob, its rim worn smooth, and a low curb around it.

moment.text: But about midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them.

next.text: Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken; and immediately all the doors were opened, and everyone’s bonds were loosened.

payload.name: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)
payload.note: Pharisee from Tarsus who persecutes the Way, is converted on the road to Damascus, and becomes the apostle Paul; told apart from the king by his Pharisee and Tarsus background and conversion narrative in Acts.

stages.label: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)

quotes.quote: The witnesses placed their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
They led him by the hand and brought him into Damascus.
I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees.
But I was born a Roman.

stages.text: Saul/Paul: man in his thirties to fifties, middle height and spare, wiry build worn by travel and hardship. Olive-brown skin, dark hair cropped short, close-trimmed dark beard with grey beginning at the chin. Lined forehead, deep-set dark eyes, strong nose. Signature outfit: plain undyed wool tunic in ochre-brown under a dark brown travelling cloak with a fringed hem. Signature prop: a worn leather writing satchel and a plain wooden walking staff.

payload.name: Silas (Silvanus)
payload.note: Jerusalem brother and companion of Paul in Acts and the letters, also named Silvanus in the epistles; all four entries are the same missionary companion, so join them into one cluster.

stages.label: Silas (Silvanus), missionary companion

quotes.quote: Silas, chief men among the brothers.
Judas and Silas, also being prophets themselves

stages.text: Silas (Silvanus): a man in his thirties, of medium height and sturdy build from travel. Olive skin, dark curly hair cropped short above the ears, a close-cut beard. Calm, steady eyes and a weathered, earnest face. Wears a plain undyed linen tunic with a dark brown woollen cloak thrown over the shoulders. Carries a traveller's leather satchel and a wooden staff.

payload.name: the Philippian jailer
payload.note: Jailer at Philippi who is converted after the earthquake.

stages.label: The Philippian jailer

quotes.quote: they threw them into prison, charging the jailer to keep them safely
drew his sword and was about to kill himself

stages.text: The Philippian jailer: a man of about forty, sturdy and weathered, with a dark beard cropped close and short dark hair. Olive-brown skin, broad brow, steady grey-brown eyes. He wears a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist over a short ochre-brown cloak, and military-style sandals. He carries a Roman short sword at his hip, and a heavy iron key ring at his belt.

payload.name: Philippi
payload.note: The Roman colony in Macedonia where Lydia is converted and Paul and Silas are jailed in Acts, and the city addressed by Paul's letter to the Philippians; the same city across all three entries, so all three keys belong together.

stages.label: Philippi

quotes.quote: Philippi, which is a city of Macedonia, the foremost of the district, a Roman colony.

stages.text: Philippi: a Roman colony on a low plain of Macedonia, ringed by green hills and fertile fields. Stone walls and a forum of pale limestone with colonnades, red-tiled roofs, Roman temples on rising ground, and a broad paved road. Olive trees, cypress and plane trees line the streets; a river runs near the city gate where people gather to pray.

moment.text: He said, “You are blessed by Yahweh, my daughter. You have shown more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning, because you didn’t follow young men, whether poor or rich.

previous.text: He said, “Who are you?” She answered, “I am Ruth your servant. Therefore spread the corner of your garment over your servant; for you are a near kinsman.”

next.text: Now, my daughter, don’t be afraid. I will do to you all that you say; for all the city of my people knows that you are a worthy woman.

payload.name: Ruth
payload.note: Moabite widow of Mahlon who goes with Naomi to Bethlehem, gleans in Boaz's field, becomes Boaz's wife and mother of Obed.

stages.label: Ruth

quotes.quote: The name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the other was Ruth.
It is the Moabite lady who came back with Naomi out of the country of Moab.

stages.text: Ruth: a young woman in her twenties; slender, sturdy build from field labour; warm olive-brown skin; dark hair worn covered with a linen head-veil in the fields and bound back at home; calm, steady face with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a rust-red wool cloak over the shoulders, belted with a cord. Carries a simple woven gleaner's basket on one arm.

payload.name: Boaz
payload.note: Wealthy kinsman of Elimelech in Bethlehem who shows kindness to Ruth, redeems the land and marries her; the one who acts as redeemer at the city gate.

stages.label: Boaz

quotes.quote: a mighty man of wealth, of the family of Elimelech, and his name was Boaz.
Boaz went up to the gate and sat down there.

stages.text: Boaz: a mature man in his middle years, broad-shouldered and sturdy, of a prosperous landholder. Olive-brown skin weathered by the fields. Dark hair and a short, neatly trimmed beard with some grey at the temples. Calm, dignified face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long undertunic of undyed linen under a cloak of deep blue wool with a woven band at the hem. Carries a shepherd's staff of olive wood.

payload.name: Naomi
payload.note: Wife of Elimelech, mother of Mahlon and Chilion, mother-in-law of Ruth and Orpah; returns from Moab to Bethlehem and calls herself Mara; cares for Ruth's son.

stages.label: Naomi

quotes.quote: The name of the man was Elimelech, and the name of his wife Naomi.
Call me Mara, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.
I went out full, and Yahweh has brought me home again empty.
Naomi took the child, laid him in her bosom, and became nurse to him.

stages.text: Naomi: woman of middle years, mature and weathered by grief; lean, upright build; olive skin with sun-darkened forearms; dark hair covered by a plain linen veil, with grey threads showing at the temples; lined face, dignified and steady; wears an undyed brown woollen tunic with a long dull-ochre cloak over it, belted at the waist; carries a small water skin or walking staff alone.

payload.name: Threshing floor of Boaz (Ruth)
payload.note: Threshing floor where Boaz winnows barley and Ruth lies at his feet; distinct from the Jebusite threshing floors because it is in Bethlehem and tied to Ruth's story.

stages.label: Threshing floor of Boaz

quotes.quote: he will be winnowing barley tonight on the threshing floor.
She went down to the threshing floor

stages.text: Threshing floor of Boaz: a flat, beaten-earth threshing floor on a rise above Bethlehem's fields, swept hard and pale under the open sky. Low stone walls mark its edge, with a heap of threshed barley grain and chaff at one side and a wooden winnowing fork leaning against a standing sheaf. Barley fields and scattered olive trees stretch beyond, and the distant town walls of Bethlehem show on the horizon.

payload.name: Naomi's house in Bethlehem
payload.note: Ruth and Naomi's home in Bethlehem where the child is cared for; distinct from Boaz's fields and the threshing floor.

stages.label: Naomi's house in Bethlehem

quotes.quote: each of you in the house of her husband
except that she rested a little in the house
the woman who has come into your house

stages.text: Naomi's house in Bethlehem: a modest village dwelling of mud-brick walls and a flat roof of packed earth and beams, with a low doorway and a courtyard of beaten earth. Stone terraces and olive trees stand on the hillside, with grain fields in the valley below and the walls of Bethlehem nearby.

payload.name: Near kinsman
payload.note: Unnamed closer relative who declines to redeem the land and yields his right to Boaz, giving up his sandal; distinct from Boaz, who is the one who redeems.

stages.label: Near kinsman

quotes.quote: Behold, the near kinsman of whom Boaz spoke came by.
he took off his sandal.

stages.text: Near kinsman: man in his fifties, lean and weathered, of an Israelite farming family; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and close-cropped dark hair; deep-set, serious eyes and lined brow. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a dusty ochre woollen cloak. Carries no props alone.

payload.name: Elders of Bethlehem at the gate
payload.note: Ten elders and city witnesses at the gate in Ruth who bless Ruth and Boaz.

stages.label: Elders of Bethlehem at the gate

quotes.quote: Boaz took ten men of the elders of the city, and said, “Sit down here,” and they sat down.

stages.text: Elders of Bethlehem: men of mature age, around fifty to seventy; lean to medium build; olive-brown skin; full grey-streaked beards and hair kept short under a head cloth; weathered, dignified faces. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a deep indigo-blue cloak over it, and a plain woven sash. Props: a simple wooden staff carried by each man alone.

payload.name: Bethlehem city gate
payload.note: The gate of Bethlehem where Boaz settles the redemption with the kinsman; a civic gate, not a city.

stages.label: Bethlehem city gate

quotes.quote: Now Boaz went up to the gate and sat down there.

stages.text: Bethlehem city gate: a double gateway cut into a low, thick wall of pale limestone blocks, weathered and mortared, with a flat stone bench set against the inner wall. Above it rises a rough roof of timber beams with a small guard chamber. Beyond the gate lie terraced hillsides of olive and fig trees, dry grass, and the stony road climbing toward Ephrathah.

moment.text: Now on the third day, Esther put on her royal clothing and stood in the inner court of the king’s house, next to the king’s house. The king sat on his royal throne in the royal house, next to the entrance of the house.

next.text: When the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, she obtained favor in his sight; and the king held out to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand. So Esther came near and touched the top of the scepter.

payload.name: Esther
payload.note: Jewish orphan niece of Mordecai, made queen to replace Vashti, who hides her identity and intercedes for her people in Persia; not the same as the Sheba queen or the unnamed queen of Daniel.

stages.label: Esther

quotes.quote: The maiden was fair and beautiful
he set the royal crown on her head
the king held out to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand
Esther put on her royal clothing

stages.text: Esther: a young woman of about twenty, slender and graceful in build, with warm olive-brown skin and dark hair braided and bound up beneath a fine veil. Her face is gentle and dignified, with large dark eyes and a calm, grave bearing. Her signature outfit is a long court robe of deep crimson silk with a gold-embroidered border, a gold belt, and gold bangles at the wrists. When received before the king she wears the royal crown of gold. She alone carries the king's golden scepter.

payload.name: Ahasuerus
payload.note: King of Persia and Media who deposes Vashti and marries Esther.

stages.label: Ahasuerus, King of Persia and Media

quotes.quote: wearing the royal crown, to show the people and the princes her beauty
this is Ahasuerus who reigned from India even to Ethiopia
The king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman
except those to whom the king might hold out the golden scepter

stages.text: Ahasuerus: man in his middle years, broad-shouldered and upright; dark, neatly curled beard and hair under a royal crown of gold; olive-brown skin; calm, heavy-lidded, dignified face. Signature outfit: long layered royal robe of deep purple and gold-embroidered blue over a white tunic. Signature props: a gold signet ring and a golden scepter.

payload.name: Haman
payload.note: Agagite official who plots to destroy the Jews and is hanged.

stages.label: Haman

quotes.quote: King Ahasuerus promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him
The king took his ring from his hand, and gave it to Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the Jews’ enemy.
the gallows fifty cubits high, which Haman has made for Mordecai

stages.text: Haman: a man of middle years, forties to fifties; broad-shouldered and heavy in build with a proud, upright carriage; olive-bronze skin; dark hair and a short, neatly trimmed dark beard with some grey at the chin; strong brow and a hard, watchful face. Signature outfit: a long Persian court robe of deep crimson with gold embroidered borders, worn with a high felt court cap; a gold signet ring of the king on his hand. Props alone: the gold signet ring.

payload.name: Palace at Susa
payload.note: The royal palace in Susa of Ahasuerus, site of the feast, Vashti's refusal, and Esther's queenship; distinguish by its Persian setting in Susa.

stages.label: Palace at Susa

quotes.quote: Esther put on her royal clothing and stood in the inner court of the king’s house, next to the king’s house.
The king sat on his royal throne in the royal house, next to the entrance of the house.
The king arose in his wrath from the banquet of wine and went into the palace garden.
whoever, whether man or woman, comes to the king into the inner court without being called

stages.text: Palace at Susa: a vast Persian royal complex on a raised platform of sun-baked brick above the plain of Susa; tall columned halls of cedar and stone with painted glazed brick friezes in blue, ochre and white; a great gate with winged guardian figures; an inner court paved in pale stone; the king's house with a throne room near its entrance; a walled palace garden of date palms, plane trees, pools and channels of water.

aliases: the place of the banquet of wine
payload.name: The banquet hall in the palace of Esther
payload.note: The room in the Persian palace where Esther hosts banquets for the king and Haman; distinct from the king's chambers in Song of Solomon.

stages.label: The banquet hall in the palace of Esther

quotes.quote: the place of the banquet of wine; and Haman had fallen on the couch where Esther was

stages.text: The banquet hall in the palace of Esther: a long interior chamber of the Persian palace at Susa, its floor of polished stone laid in pale and dark tiles, tall columns of cedar and marble rising to a painted ceiling. Low couches with cushions of deep blue and gold line the walls, and fine linen hangings in white and purple fall between the columns. Beyond the open doors lies a palace garden with date palms and cypress.
